_README: Design spec for the 8 content hubs. Edit values here, then run:  node scripts/build-hubs.mjs   (rewrites only the <head> meta, the fonts <link>, and the :root token block of each web/hub/<slug>/index.html). Add --check to verify without writing, --deck <path> to also sync the Hub Deck artifact. Shared layout + render JS are never touched.

meta.title: AI Implementation — where small-business AI projects stall, and how to get them shipped
meta.description: Most AI projects don't fail — they stall. The nine places a small-business AI rollout breaks between the demo and production, and what to do about each.
meta.ogDescription: Where small-business AI projects stall — failed pilots, hallucinations, no adoption, broken integrations — and how to get them shipped.

tokenNotes.bg: clean daylight — not a dev console
tokenNotes.accent: deep persimmon — the one CTA (white text reads)

design.subject: A field guide for a small business that bought AI and is still waiting on results — a map of where a rollout breaks between the impressive demo and the version that runs the business. Not a vendor, not a hype site.
design.audience: SMB owner/operator mid-rollout — skeptical, often already burned by an agency that overpromised, reading for the failure that sounds like their project. Campaign keywords also reach earlier-stage 'no coding / for beginners' searchers.
design.job: Request the free stalled-pilot teardown (email capture in the report band). The deeper paid reviews start from it.
design.type: Space Grotesk (600) display — geometric, reads as engineering not editorial. Inter body for dense failure-mode copy. JetBrains Mono on every label, so the page reads as a status readout.
design.signature: The ribbon is an implementation status readout — mono stat-chips under the hero showing the vitals of a rollout that's actually shipping (pilot-to-production stall rate, time-to-value target, rollback plan, named owner, adoption cadence). The 01-09 card numbering is a real sequence: the order a rollout tends to break in.
design.risk: Daylight white + a green primary + mono labels is close to 'well-made SaaS onboarding' with no strong point of view. The mono status-readout treatment (ribbon, 01-09 numbering, code-type labels) is what keeps it specific. If it drifts bland, push the postmortem idea: red-thread margin annotations, timestamps, a reviewed/open/fixed state per failure mode.
avoided: The warm-cream + high-contrast serif + terracotta cluster
The broadsheet look — hairlines everywhere, zero radius, newspaper columns
Any 'AI' imagery — glowing brains, circuit traces, robot hands, particle fields. Zero images; the ribbon stats are the visual
Marketing voice — every label names what a person controls ('Rollback plan', 'Owner', 'Adoption'), not how the system is built
Console-navy + cyan (the original palette) — the exact look of the vendors this audience already distrusts
design.superseded: 2026-09-01 to 09-02: --bg #080c14 console navy / --sea #60a5fa signal blue / --accent #06b6d4 cyan (type unchanged). Dropped because navy+cyan is the vendors' palette and leaned on the near-black-plus-acid-accent AI default.

meta.title: The Care Gap — a philanthropist's briefing on the caregiver workforce crisis
meta.description: 9.7 million direct-care jobs open by 2034 at a median wage under $26,000. The Care Gap is the Mobility Mentor Foundation's brief for funders: the crisis in named numbers, and the four pillars that move them.
meta.ogDescription: A documented care-workforce crisis, an underserved philanthropic space, and impact you can report against an ESG framework. The briefing for foundation officers and impact investors.

tokenNotes.bg: cool report-cover grey — a policy brief, not a folder
tokenNotes.accent: data-red — the crisis figure; used once, loudly

design.subject: A philanthropist's briefing on the direct-care workforce crisis, from the Mobility Mentor Foundation — the crisis in named numbers (9.7M openings by 2034, median wage under $26K, 59% on public assistance) and the four funded pillars that move them.
design.audience: Foundation officers and impact investors under ESG/DEI reporting pressure, looking for a documented, trackable social outcome in a space with less donor competition than hunger or education.
design.job: Book a 15-minute call, or download the briefing (email capture).
design.type: Newsreader (500/600) display — a text-face serif that reads as a policy journal, not a brand. IBM Plex Sans body; IBM Plex Mono for figures and labels — an institutional, government-adjacent register.
design.signature: The vitals ribbon — the crisis stated as a strip of hard figures before any prose. The four pillars are framed as 'measurable lines the Foundation reports on', each mapped to a grant-committee metric rather than a feel-good theme.
design.risk: Cool grey + institutional blue + a lone data-red is deliberately close to a real annual report — that's the point, but it risks reading dry. The single red figure and the Newsreader serif carry the gravity; if it flattens, set one number per section large.
avoided: The manila-folder / cozy-nonprofit warm palette (the previous version)
Charity imagery — hands, faces, care-recipient photos
Advocacy-poster urgency (all-caps, exclamation, colour blocks) — the audience allocates capital, it doesn't sign petitions
design.superseded: Was manila #f4efe4 + evergreen #2f5d4f + burnt-ochre #a85f22 (Newsreader / IBM Plex kept).

meta.title: Creative Flow Guitar — a new guitar session every week
meta.description: One guitar session a week, recorded raw — the tone, the room, the take left as it happened. Download the MP3 and the live recording, study it, play along.
meta.ogDescription: A new guitar session every week. Real playing, real feel — MP3s and live recordings you can own, study, and play along with.

tokenNotes.bg: walnut / record-black — an after-dark listening room
tokenNotes.accent: worn label red — used once, loudly

design.subject: A weekly guitar session, recorded raw — the tone, the room, the take left as it happened. Download the MP3 and the live recording, study it, play along.
design.audience: Players and listeners who care about authentic sound — the acoustic / instrumental / country-rock crossover, the vinyl-resurgence and classic-rock-radio audience. High intent, tired of over-produced tutorials.
design.job: Get this week's session (download), or join the weekly (email capture).
design.type: DM Serif Display — high-contrast, poster-ish, reads like a record sleeve / liner note. Hanken Grotesk body. Space Mono for session data — key, tuning, BPM, length.
design.signature: The session-vitals ribbon — key, tuning, BPM, take length, format — set in mono like the back of a record. The whole page is an after-dark listening room: one dark walnut ground, a single tube-amp amber as primary, a worn label-red used once.
design.risk: Dark walnut + amber + a display serif can tip into 'craft coffee / whiskey brand' pastiche. It stays a music page by leading with the session data and the raw-recording promise, not mood.
avoided: The warm-linen 'studio daylight' light palette (the previous version)
Guitar-hero imagery — stage lights, silhouettes, close-ups of hands on a fretboard
Streaming-service UI — play buttons, waveforms, gradient cover art
design.superseded: Was warm linen #e9e5dd + oxblood #6e2231 + brass-gold #c9a13c, Newsreader display.

meta.title: Home Services — one person for repairs, the yard, the pets, and the house while you're away (Northern California)
meta.description: Small repairs a contractor won't come for, seasonal yard work, pet and property care, and house-sitting while you travel — from one reliable person. Paid, work-trade, or a mix. Northern California.
meta.ogDescription: One person for the house stuff — small repairs, the yard, the pets, and watching the place while you're away. Northern California.

tokenNotes.bg: primed drywall — a clean job, warm white

design.subject: One reliable person for the house stuff in Northern California: small repairs under the ~$1,000 licensing threshold, honey-do lists, seasonal yard work — plus house, pet, and property care while you travel. Paid, work-trade, or a mix.
design.audience: NorCal homeowners who can't get a licensed contractor to call back for a small job, and who juggle a separate pet sitter, dog walker, and house-checker when they travel. Ranges from ordinary households to owners of second homes and estates (the premium tier).
design.job: Get on the schedule — an enquiry for a job, or for house / pet / property sitting.
design.type: Familjen Grotesk display — a sturdy, plainspoken grotesk. Hanken Grotesk body. Space Mono for the service list and terms.
design.signature: The scope ribbon states the boundary out loud — 'under the licensing threshold, no permit required, one person not a rotating cast, keys you hand over and stop thinking about.' The offer cards are the actual jobs, priced plainly.
design.risk: Slate-blue + safety-orange on drywall-white can read as a generic trades-directory template. The plain-spoken 'one person for the house stuff' voice and the honest scope boundary keep it specific.
avoided: The manila + hunter-green 'farmhouse' palette (the previous version)
Tool close-ups, hard-hat stock photos, before/after grids
Handyman-app aesthetics — star ratings, dispatch maps, surge-style urgency

meta.title: Mountainwize — purpose coaching for men who got everything right
meta.description: Therapy got you functional. This is the part after. Structured purpose coaching for men over 40, run by someone who has actually been lost, actually lost the money, and actually found the way through.
meta.ogDescription: Purpose coaching for men over 40 who did everything right and still feel the gap. Lived, consequence-earned — not another framework from someone who's never risked anything.

tokenNotes.accent: the route line — used once, on the CTA

design.subject: Purpose coaching for men over 40 who did everything right — career, family, money — and still feel the gap where a reason should be. The coach is Evan, 'the mountain man'; his credibility is lived, consequence-earned experience, not a certification.
design.audience: Men 38-60 who've tried therapy, journaling, meditation and found them insufficient. Skeptical of the coaching industry. Ready to buy a structured path, not read more.
design.job: Take the free assessment (email capture) — it sorts what they're actually dealing with and points them to the right route.
design.type: Bitter (500/600/700) display — a slab serif with spine, reads as a field guide written by someone who did it, not wellness-soft. Inter body. Space Mono for route data — session length, price, weeks, terms.
design.signature: The route. The page is structured and named like a climb — the ribbon is 'route beta' (a conditions strip), and the offer section is four routes graded by where you are (Recon free, 4-week Reset, flagship climb, group rope team), not sorted by price. Hero: 'Therapy got you functional. This is the part after.'
design.risk: Slab serif + paper + brick-red can drift toward a generic 'rugged outdoors brand' (REI-adjacent). Mitigation: precise and quiet — zero images, no mountain silhouettes or textures; the route language does the work. If revisited: drop the warm accent for a high-altitude ice-blue and lean harder on the topo/elevation motif as a drawn element.
avoided: The wellness cluster: soft sans, sage/blush, gradient blobs, lowercase, 'journey' language — the exact aesthetic the campaign positions against
The biohacking / tech-dark cluster: near-black ground, neon accent, data UI
The three AI defaults (cream+serif+terracotta / near-black+acid / broadsheet hairlines)
Any photograph of a mountain, a pensive man at a view, or a summit
design.superseded: 2026-09-02: --bg was #f3f0e8 warm topo paper; pulled cold to #edf0f0, --deep deepened, per the risk note above.

meta.title: Build Watcher — independent owner's representation for construction projects
meta.description: Your architect manages design; your GC manages their margin. Build Watcher manages the budget, schedule, scope and risk for the owner, from feasibility through closeout.
meta.ogDescription: Independent owner's representation for construction projects. Someone watching the build for you — and only you.

tokenNotes.bg: deep cyanotype — a night jobsite, watched
tokenNotes.accent: redline / markup orange — used once, loudly

design.subject: An owner's representative for a construction project — the one party at the table working only for the owner. Manages budget, schedule, scope and risk from feasibility through closeout, separate from the architect and the GC.
design.audience: An owner about to build, or mid-build, who senses the architect manages design and the GC manages their own margin, and no one is minding the owner's exposure.
design.job: Get the free owner's checklist (email capture), or book a project review.
design.type: Archivo display — a structural grotesk with tight caps, reads as drafting / spec. Hanken Grotesk body. Space Mono for the checklist and figures.
design.signature: A cyanotype night-jobsite — the page is a dark instrument panel with drafting-cyan linework and a single redline-orange for the markup. The free 'checklist' is framed as the 18 things an owner should have locked before a shovel moves — the same review the paid engagements start from.
design.risk: Dark blue + cyan + orange is close to a generic 'construction-tech' dashboard. The redline-markup language and the owner's-side-of-the-table framing keep it from being SaaS.
avoided: The pale blueprint-paper palette (the previous version)
Hero shots of cranes, hard hats, or finished buildings
Contractor-marketing warmth — family photos, 'your dream home'
design.superseded: Was blueprint paper #eceef1 + navy #22436e + redline-orange #c2410c (Archivo kept).

meta.title: Sunflower Acres — a wheelchair-accessible flower farm in Concord, California
meta.description: Step-free into and through the fields. Accessible parking and restrooms, loaner wheelchairs on site, companions free. Come cut your own flowers in Concord, CA.
meta.ogDescription: A wheelchair-accessible flower farm in Concord, California. The same day at the farm, for everyone.

tokenNotes.bg: warm sunlight on a clear day
tokenNotes.ink: rich soil brown-black — high contrast on purpose
tokenNotes.accent: deep seed-head gold — carries white button text; used once, loudly

design.subject: A wheelchair-accessible flower farm in Concord, California — step-free paths into and through the fields, accessible parking and restrooms, loaner wheelchairs on site, companions admitted free. U-pick, bouquets, dried arrangements, subscriptions, workshops, private group bookings.
design.audience: Bay Area adults planning an outing for a group that includes a wheelchair user or someone with limited mobility — often an adult child planning for a parent, or a parent of a disabled kid — plus East Bay flower lovers and care / day-program coordinators within about an hour of Concord.
design.job: Book a visit, or get the free accessible-visit guide (email capture).
design.type: Fraunces display — a soft optical serif, warm and human, made by people not a chain. Hanken Grotesk body. Space Mono for hours, prices, and access details.
design.signature: Accessibility stated plainly and first — the ribbon is the access facts (step-free paths, accessible parking + restrooms, loaner chairs, companions free), because every competitor makes you call ahead and guess. Ink-on-ground contrast is deliberately high for low-vision visitors.
design.risk: Warm sun-white + leaf-green + gold is the one hub that stays in warm-light territory. It differentiates on being unambiguously the sunny, accessible one — and on access-first content — rather than on palette novelty.
avoided: The pale-field-green wash (the previous version) — not enough contrast for the audience
Rustic farm-stand clutter — chalkboards, burlap, mason jars
Inspiration-porn disability imagery
design.superseded: Was pale field-green #eef1e1 + field-green #3d6b2b + bright gold #efa100; ground warmed, ink deepened for contrast, accent darkened to a seed-head gold that carries white button text.

meta.title: Surf Vacations — trip reports, break intel, charter logistics
meta.description: Where the swell is and how to get there. Season timing, honest charter costs, and uncrowded breaks for surfers who plan around the forecast.
meta.ogDescription: Trip reports, break guides, and charter logistics for surfers who plan around forecasts, not calendars.

tokenNotes.bg: pushed from the Content Hubs tab (2026-09-02)

design.subject: Trip reports, break intel, and charter logistics for surfers who plan around the forecast, not the calendar — where the swell is, season timing, honest charter costs, uncrowded breaks.
design.audience: Surfers who read swell models and book around a window — not beginners looking for a resort package (though a beginner tier exists).
design.job: Get the weekly report (email capture), or browse the trips.
design.type: Bricolage Grotesque display — a lively contemporary grotesk with optical sizing. Hanken Grotesk body. Space Mono for dates, costs, and swell data.
design.signature: The conditions ribbon reads like a forecast strip. The whole page is a cool tide-chart / almanac, not a travel brochure — sea-mist ground, ocean-teal primary, a buoy-orange hazard accent used once.
design.risk: Cool mist + teal + orange is a restrained, chart-like palette; the risk is it reads under-designed. The forecast-strip framing and the honest-cost copy are what make it deliberate.
avoided: The warm-sand 'beach resort' palette (the previous version)
Drone barrel shots, sunset silhouettes, palm trees
Booking-engine UI — price sliders, calendar grids, 'only 2 left'
design.superseded: Was warm sand #f3efe4 + ocean-teal #0e6e7d + sunset-orange #e4572e (Bricolage kept).
